chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from Bukayr ibn Aʿyan, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said:
“If the hadath occurs in the mosque, then there is no harm in performing wudu (ablution) in the mosque.”

key_terms.الْحَدَثُ: a state of ritual impurity that necessitates purification
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the place where the ruling is being applied
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing for taharah
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform wudu (ablution) in the mosque if hadath occurs there?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity in the mosque. It states that if a state of hadath occurs while one is in the mosque, there is no objection to performing wudu (ablution) there.
